classification.difficultyReason: Combine parallel and perpendicular equations, their intersection and distances to obtain base times height.

content.prompt: The diagram shows a parallelogram $ABCD$ in which $A$ is the point with coordinates $(8,3)$, $B$ is the point with coordinates $(2,7)$ and $C$ is the point with coordinates $(12,12)$. $X$ is a point on $BC$ such that $AX$ is perpendicular to $BC$. Find:

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12, diagram to the right of the stem
spec.description: Unshaded coordinate diagram with arrowed axes, no ticks or grid, labelled vertices A, B, C and D, and all four parallelogram edges. Ordinary edges and point markers use black under house style. The source origin label is omitted under the graph convention. Neither X nor AX is supplied.
spec.mathematics: A=(8,3), B=(2,7), C=(12,12). D is positioned at A+C-B=(18,8) to construct the parallelogram, without printing its coordinates. AD is parallel to BC and AB is parallel to CD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no perpendicular foot, altitude, calculated equations or lengths are shown.

answer.worked:
$AD\parallel BC$, so their gradients are equal.

$$\begin{align*}m_{AD}&=\frac{12-7}{12-2}\\m_{AD}&=\frac12\\y-3&=\frac12(x-8)\\y-3&=\frac12x-4\\y&=\frac12x-1\end{align*}$$

$AX\perp BC$, so its gradient is the negative reciprocal of $\frac12$.

$$\begin{align*}m_{AX}&=-2\\y-3&=-2(x-8)\\y-3&=-2x+16\\y&=-2x+19\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$X\left(\frac{26}{5},\frac{43}{5}\right)$.

Solve the equations of $BC$ and $AX$ simultaneously.
answer.worked:
For $BC$:

$$\begin{align*}y-7&=\frac12(x-2)\\y&=\frac12x+6\end{align*}$$

At $X$, the equations of $BC$ and $AX$ give:

$$\begin{align*}\frac12x+6&=-2x+19\\\frac52x&=13\\x&=\frac{26}{5}\\y&=-2\left(\frac{26}{5}\right)+19\\y&=\frac{43}{5}\end{align*}$$

Check in $BC$: $\frac12\left(\frac{26}{5}\right)+6=\frac{43}{5}$. Thus $X=\left(\frac{26}{5},\frac{43}{5}\right)$.

answer.short:
$70$ square units.

Use $BC$ as the base and $AX$ as its perpendicular height.
answer.worked:
$AX\perp BC$, so $AX$ is the perpendicular height corresponding to base $BC$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=BC\times AX\\\text{Area}&=5\sqrt5\times\frac{14\sqrt5}{5}\\\text{Area}&=70\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
